blocks.text: Explains why this is its own module (testability, shared by Parts 3 and 4), lists the three conservative design choices (resolve symlinks, reject broad roots, commonpath not string-prefix), and identifies this as an F2 Part 1 artefact.
blocks.title: Module docstring

blocks.anchor: # Roots we refuse to accept as the configured allowed folder, even if
blocks.text: _DISALLOWED_ROOTS is a frozenset built at import time from '/' and Path.home(), each resolved; paths that do not exist are excluded. PathGuardError is a plain Exception subclass with no extra fields — the message carries all context.
blocks.title: _DISALLOWED_ROOTS and PathGuardError

blocks.text: Resolves root with expanduser/resolve, then checks in order: exists, is a directory, not in _DISALLOWED_ROOTS. Returns the resolved Path on success. This is the stricter check; it additionally rejects non-existent or non-directory roots, unlike is_within_root.
blocks.title: Root validation at startup

blocks.anchor: def is_within_root(candidate: str | Path, root: Path) -> bool:
blocks.text: Resolves the candidate (swallowing OSError/RuntimeError and returning False). Returns True if resolved_candidate equals root or if os.path.commonpath of the two paths equals str(root). The root argument is assumed to already be the validated Path from assert_safe_root.
blocks.title: Containment predicate

blocks.anchor: def assert_within_root(candidate: str | Path, root: Path) -> Path:
blocks.text: Calls is_within_root on the resolved candidate and raises PathGuardError with both the candidate's resolved path and the root in the message if containment fails. Returns the resolved candidate on success. This is the function Parts 3 and 4 should call.
blocks.title: Raising containment check

gotchas: assert_safe_root rejects '/' and the user's home directory as roots — this catches misconfigured daemon installs, not deliberate overrides
is_within_root returns False for unresolvable paths (symlink loops, OSError) — never treats them as safe
os.path.commonpath is used rather than a string prefix so '/home/user/project-x' is not falsely inside '/home/user/project'
how_it_works: At import time, _DISALLOWED_ROOTS is built from '/' and Path.home() (resolved), creating a frozenset of forbidden root values
assert_safe_root is called once at startup to validate the configured root; it resolves symlinks, checks existence and directory-ness, and rejects any root in _DISALLOWED_ROOTS
is_within_root resolves the candidate with expanduser/resolve and uses os.path.commonpath to verify containment — not a string prefix check
assert_within_root wraps is_within_root and raises PathGuardError with a descriptive message on failure, so rejections are always loud and logged
inputs: root: str | Path (the configured allowed folder)
candidate: str | Path (a path to validate)
purpose: Every read, write, delete, and execute operation in the daemon must route its path through this module before touching disk. It is a standalone module (not a method on the daemon class) so Parts 3 and 4 can both import it and it can be unit-tested without any WebSocket or event-loop code.
side_effects: _DISALLOWED_ROOTS is built at import time by calling Path.resolve() on '/' and home()
summary: Containment-boundary module that validates the allowed-root folder and enforces that every file path stays inside it.

symbols.details: Stricter than is_within_root: also rejects roots that do not exist, are not directories, or resolve to '/' or the home directory.
